full_text_en:
Changchun Taiheng Housing Development Co., Ltd. v. Changchun Municipal Bureau of Planning and Natural Resources — dispute over state-owned land use right transfer contract

[Ruling Summary]

1. Where a contract cannot be performed due to the promulgation of national laws, regulations, or policies, and as a result, one party's purpose in entering into the contract cannot be achieved, and that party requests the court to rescind the contract, the people's court shall support such request.

2. Given that both parties are not at fault for the inability to perform the contract and the failure to achieve one party's contractual purpose, in accordance with Article 97 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the court may only order the return of the price paid and the corresponding fruits, and shall not support a claim for compensation for losses by one party against the other.

3. Where a party has incurred deed tax losses for the purpose of performing the contract, and neither party is at fault for the rescission of the contract in question, such losses may be shared equally between the parties based on the principle of fairness.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2019) Supreme People's Court Civil Retrial No. 246

Retrial Applicant (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Changchun Taiheng Housing Development Co., Ltd. Address: No. 1048, Taiyuan East Street, Economic Development Zone, Changchun City, Jilin Province.

Legal Representative: Hu Shoudong, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Ma Liyan, lawyer at Beijing Dacheng (Changchun) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Yu Mengna, lawyer at Beijing Dacheng (Changchun) Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Changchun Municipal Bureau of Planning and Natural Resources. Address: No. 3066, South Ring Road, Nanguan District, Changchun City, Jilin Province.

Legal Representative: Qu Guohui, Director of the Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Teng Dali, staff member of the Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Linbo, staff member of the Bureau.

The retrial applicant, Changchun Taiheng Housing Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Taiheng Company), in a dispute with the respondent, Changchun Municipal Bureau of Planning and Natural Resources (hereinafter referred to as Changchun Natural Resources Bureau), over a state-owned land use right transfer contract, refused to accept the civil judgment (2018) Ji Min Zhong No. 264 rendered by the Jilin High People's Court, and applied to this Court for retrial. This Court rendered the civil ruling (2019) Supreme People's Court Min Shen No. 1425 on May 30, 2019, granting the retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing on November 11, 2019. Ma Liyan and Yu Mengna, agents ad litem of Taiheng Company, and Teng Dali and Jiang Linbo, agents ad litem of Changchun Natural Resources Bureau, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case is now concluded.

Taiheng Company alleged at the first instance: On November 25, 2010, Taiheng Company entered into a "State-owned Construction Land Use Right Transfer Contract" with the Changchun Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources (hereinafter referred to as Changchun Municipal Land Bureau). During the performance of the contract in question, the State Council promulgated the "Regulations on the Expropriation and Compensation of Houses on State-owned Land," which made it impossible for Taiheng Company to perform its obligations of demolishing above-ground structures and providing compensation as stipulated in the contract. Based on the principle of change of circumstances, Taiheng Company requested rescission of the contract in question. In summary, the claims were: 1. Rescind the "State-owned Construction Land Use Right Transfer Contract" in question; 2. Order Changchun Municipal Land Bureau to return the land transfer fee of RMB 26,300,000; 3. Order Changchun Municipal Land Bureau to compensate Taiheng Company for the deed tax paid, RMB 1,315,000; 4. Order Changchun Municipal Land Bureau to pay interest of RMB 9,836,491.34 (calculated as of December 31, 2016, and from January 1, 2017, until the full return of the land transfer fee, calculated at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period).

Changchun Municipal Land Bureau argued: First, there is no factual basis or condition for the application of the change of circumstances principle in this case. Taiheng Company's request to rescind the contract based on the change of circumstances principle is intended to shift investment risk and evade contractual liability. Second, the implementation of the "Regulations on the Expropriation and Compensation of Houses on State-owned Land" did not cause a material change in the objective circumstances on which the contract in question depended, and did not affect Taiheng Company's ability to achieve its contractual purpose. This case does not meet the conditions for applying the change of circumstances principle. Third, Taiheng Company was negligent in failing to apply for a demolition permit in a timely manner, resulting in its inability to carry out the demolition after the implementation of the "Regulations on the Expropriation and Compensation of Houses on State-owned Land." Taiheng Company is at fault for the obstacle to contract performance.

The first instance court found the following facts upon trial: On October 18, 2010, Changchun Municipal Land Bureau published a listing announcement for the transfer of Plot B, located east of the existing residential area in Kuancheng District, south of Changchun No. 25 Middle School, west of Changnong Highway, and north of the vacant lot, with plot number 57-130-5, transfer area of 21,632 square meters. The announcement stated: The land in question was transferred in its current condition, including land that had already been demolished and land that had not been demolished within the planned land boundary and the current land consolidation boundary. The successful bidder for the land not yet demolished was responsible for its own demolition and consolidation after acquiring the land, and all related costs were to be borne by the successful bidder.

On November 22, 2010, Taiheng Company submitted a "Bidding Quotation Form" to Changchun Municipal Land Bureau, applying to participate in the listing transfer of the land in question, and committed to fully accept and comply with the provisions and requirements of the listing documents. On the same day, Taiheng Company paid a bid deposit of RMB 6,000,000 to Changchun Municipal Land Bureau. On November 25, 2010, Changchun Municipal Land Bureau and Taiheng Company signed a "Transaction Confirmation Letter," confirming that Taiheng Company had won the bid for the land in question.

On November 25, 2010, Changchun Municipal Land Bureau, as the transferor, and Taiheng Company, as the transferee, signed a "State-owned Construction Land Use Right Transfer Contract," with the main terms: 1. The plot number of the transferred land was 57-130-5, with an area of 21,632 square meters. The transferor agreed to deliver the land to the transferee before November 25, 2010. The land was delivered in its current condition, meaning that the successful bidder for the land and above-ground structures not yet demolished was responsible for the demolition and compensation consolidation; 2. The transfer price was RMB 26,300,000, payable in a lump sum within 30 days from the date of signing the contract; 3. The transferee agreed that the construction project on the land in question should commence before November 25, 2011, and be completed before November 25, 2013. If the transferee terminated the project investment and construction for its own reasons, and requested to terminate the contract and return the land, the transferor would, after obtaining approval from the people's government that originally approved the land transfer plan, return all or part of the state-owned construction land use right transfer fee (without interest) excluding the deposit as stipulated in the contract, recover the state-owned construction land use right, and provide no compensation for buildings, structures, and ancillary facilities already built on the land. The transferor could also require the transferee to clear the built buildings, structures, and ancillary facilities to restore the site to level condition; however, if the transferor was willing to continue using the built buildings, structures, and ancillary facilities on the land, it would provide certain compensation to the transferee.

On December 24, 2010, Taiheng Company paid a land transfer fee of RMB 20,300,000 to Changchun Municipal Land Bureau.

On January 21, 2011, the State Council issued the "Regulations on the Expropriation and Compensation of Houses on State-owned Land," which provided in Article 4 that the municipal or county people's government is responsible for house expropriation and compensation work within its administrative region. The house expropriation department designated by the municipal or county people's government organizes and implements the house expropriation and compensation work within its administrative region. Municipal and county people's governments shall cooperate with each other to ensure the smooth progress of house expropriation and compensation work in accordance with the provisions of these regulations and the division of duties prescribed by the people's government at the corresponding level.

On September 26, 2012, Taiheng Company paid deed tax of RMB 1,315,000.

The first instance court held that the "State-owned Construction Land Use Right Transfer Contract" in question was the true expression of the parties' intentions, did not violate mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, and was legal and valid. When the parties signed the contract on November 25, 2010, Taiheng Company was aware that it would be responsible for the demolition and consolidation of the land and above-ground structures. After signing the contract, it should bear the commercial risk of performing the demolition itself. Continuing to perform the "State-owned Construction Land Use Right Transfer Contract" between the parties did not show any obvious unfairness. If Taiheng Company had actively applied for a demolition permit after acquiring the land on November 25, 2010, it would have been eligible as a demolition entity under the regulations. If its failure to apply for a house demolition permit in a timely manner led to the current inability to demolish, the consequences should be borne by itself. Accordingly, the first instance court ruled: Dismiss Taiheng Company's claims.

Taiheng Company appealed, arguing: First, the "State-owned Construction Land Use Right Transfer Contract" in question stipulated that Changchun Municipal Land Bureau transferred the land to Taiheng Company by way of "raw land." The promulgation of the "Regulations on the Expropriation and Compensation of Houses on State-owned Land" made it impossible to continue performing the contract, thereby frustrating the purpose of Taiheng Company in signing the contract. Second, the promulgation and implementation of the "Regulations on the Expropriation and Compensation of Houses on State-owned Land" were not attributable to either party. The first instance court incorrectly found that the policy change was a commercial risk to be borne by Taiheng Company. Third, according to the provisions of the "State-owned Construction Land Use Right Transfer Contract," Taiheng Company's time for performing the demolition was one year, and Taiheng Company was not negligent in performing its contractual obligations. On September 21, 2010, the Ministry of Land and Resources and the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development jointly issued the "Notice of the Ministry of Land and Resources and the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development on Further Strengthening the Regulation of Real Estate Land and Construction Management," which clearly required that land should not be transferred in the form of "raw land." Under these circumstances, Changchun Municipal Land Bureau still transferred the land in question in the form of "raw land," causing the contract to be unperformable, for which Changchun Municipal Land Bureau was at fault. In summary, Taiheng Company requested the revocation of the first instance judgment and a new judgment in favor of its claim.

Changchun Municipal Land Bureau responded: First, there is no factual basis or condition for applying the change of circumstances principle in this case. The "State-owned Construction Land Use Right Transfer Contract" in question is legal and valid, and the implementation of the "Regulations on the Expropriation and Compensation of Houses on State-owned Land" does not affect Taiheng Company's acquisition of the land use right in question. Second, the adjustment of national policies on land demolition and consolidation is not an unforeseeable fact. As a professional real estate development enterprise, Taiheng Company had sufficient knowledge of the trend in land demolition and consolidation policies. Therefore, the inability to perform demolition and consolidation due to policy changes falls within the category of commercial risk borne by Taiheng Company. Third, continuing to perform the "State-owned Construction Land Use Right Transfer Contract" would not result in manifest unfairness, and Taiheng Company's contractual purpose has not been frustrated. In summary, Changchun Municipal Land Bureau requested the dismissal of Taiheng Company's appeal.

The second instance court held: The purpose of Taiheng Company in signing the "State-owned Construction Land Use Right Transfer Contract" was to obtain the land use right. Changchun Municipal Land Bureau had delivered the land in question to Taiheng Company as agreed, and at the time of delivery, it complied with the laws and policies then in effect, with no obstacles to the realization of the contractual purpose. The "Notice of the Ministry of Land and Resources and the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development on Further Strengthening the Regulation of Real Estate Land and Construction Management," jointly issued on September 21, 2010, clearly required that land should not be transferred in the form of "raw land." As a professional real estate development enterprise, Taiheng Company should have foreseen at the time of signing the contract that there might be commercial risks that could prevent the full realization of the contractual purpose during the performance of the contract. The "Regulations on the Expropriation and Compensation of Houses on State-owned Land" was issued nearly two months after the parties signed the contract. During this period, Taiheng Company faced no obstacle in applying for a demolition permit. Even after the issuance of the regulations, Taiheng Company could still negotiate with Changchun Municipal Land Bureau regarding the demolition and consolidation. The "Regulations on the Expropriation and Compensation of Houses on State-owned Land" only affected the specific method of performing the demolition and consolidation obligations under the transfer contract; the objective circumstances on which the contract depended, such as the land use right transfer and land development, did not change, and the regulations did not necessarily frustrate Taiheng Company's contractual purpose. Although Taiheng Company claimed that it had repeatedly requested government authorities to carry out the demolition and consolidation, it failed to provide evidence to prove this. Therefore, the claim was not accepted. Accordingly, the second instance court ruled: Dismiss the appeal and uphold the original judgment.

Taiheng Company applied for retrial, arguing: First, the original courts incorrectly held that this case did not constitute a change of circumstances, resulting in an error in the application of law. The "State-owned Construction Land Use Right Transfer Contract" in question stipulated that Changchun Municipal Land Bureau transferred the land by way of "raw land." Subsequently, the State Council's promulgation of the "Regulations on the Expropriation and Compensation of Houses on State-owned Land" clearly provided that the municipal or county people's government is responsible for house expropriation and compensation work within its administrative region. This policy change rendered Taiheng Company unable to carry out the demolition and consolidation of the land in question as stipulated in the contract. Taiheng Company could not have foreseen the policy change, and due to reasons not attributable to either party, the contract in question could not continue to be performed, thereby frustrating the contractual purpose. Second, the demolition period stipulated in the contract in question ran from November 25, 2010, to November 25, 2011. Since the State Council issued the "Regulations on the Expropriation and Compensation of Houses on State-owned Land" on January 21, 2011, a policy change occurred just two months after the contract was signed, making it impossible for Taiheng Company to apply for a demolition permit. The original court incorrectly held that Taiheng Company's failure to actively apply for a demolition permit led to the inability to demolish, and found that Taiheng Company bore the responsibility for the inability to demolish. Third, Changchun Municipal Land Bureau was at fault for the signing and inability to perform the contract. As the land transfer authority, Changchun Municipal Land Bureau should have had full knowledge and understanding of relevant policies and documents. The "Notice on Further Strengthening the Regulation of Real Estate Land and Construction Management," issued by the Ministry of Land and Resources and the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development on September 21, 2010, clearly stipulated that land should not be transferred in the form of "raw land." After the issuance of this document, Changchun Municipal Land Bureau still transferred the land by way of "raw land" and signed the contract in question with Taiheng Company. Therefore, Changchun Municipal Land Bureau was at fault for the inability to perform the contract. In summary, Taiheng Company requested: Revoke the first and second instance judgments and issue a new judgment in favor of all of Taiheng Company's claims; litigation costs to be borne by Changchun Municipal Land Bureau.

Changchun Municipal Land Bureau responded: This case lacks the factual basis and conditions for applying the change of circumstances principle. Taiheng Company's request to rescind the contract based on the change of circumstances principle lacks factual and legal support. First, the objective circumstances on which the contract depended did not undergo a material change. The purpose of Taiheng Company in signing the contract was to obtain the land use right. The provision regarding demolition and consolidation by Taiheng Company was merely an agreement on the post-transfer demolition matters and did not affect Taiheng Company's purpose of obtaining the land use right. Second, as a professional real estate development enterprise, Taiheng Company should have been aware of the state's adjustments to land demolition policies. Such policy changes fall within the commercial risk to be borne by Taiheng Company. After the contract was signed, Taiheng Company was negligent in applying for a demolition permit, resulting in its inability to carry out the demolition on its own, and it should bear the adverse consequences. Third, the "Regulations on the Expropriation and Compensation of Houses on State-owned Land" came into effect on January 21, 2011. Taiheng Company did not sue for rescission until 2017, and its right to rescind had long expired. In summary, Changchun Municipal Land Bureau requested the dismissal of Taiheng Company's retrial application and the upholding of the original judgment.

During the retrial, this Court found: Changchun Municipal Land Bureau was renamed Changchun Municipal Bureau of Planning and Natural Resources on May 10, 2019.

Both parties had no objection to the facts found by the first and second instance courts, and this Court confirms them.

This Court holds: Based on the parties' arguments, the issues in dispute in this case are: (1) whether the "State-owned Construction Land Use Right Transfer Contract" in question should be rescinded; and (2) if rescinded, the determination of liability after rescission. Regarding these issues, this Court's analysis is as follows:

(1) Whether the "State-owned Construction Land Use Right Transfer Contract" in question should be rescinded

The "State-owned Construction Land Use Right Transfer Contract" signed by Changchun Municipal Land Bureau and Taiheng Company on November 25, 2010, was the true expression of the parties' intentions, did not violate mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, and was legally valid. The contract in question stipulated that the state-owned construction land use right was transferred by way of "raw land," and the portion of above-ground structures not yet demolished was the responsibility of Taiheng Company. Within two months after the signing of the contract, the State Council issued the "Regulations on the Expropriation and Compensation of Houses on State-owned Land" on January 21, 2011, which explicitly provided that the municipal or county people's government is responsible for house expropriation and compensation work within its administrative region. As a result, due to the promulgation of these regulations, Taiheng Company was unable to obtain the status of a demolition entity and could not complete the demolition and consolidation of the land in question as stipulated in the contract. After more than seven years of coordination with Changchun Natural Resources Bureau, Taiheng Company remained unable to resolve the demolition issue concerning the land. In this regard, Taiheng Company's filing of a lawsuit with the people's court to rescind the contract did not exceed the time limit for such rescission. Changchun Natural Resources Bureau's defense that Taiheng Company's request for rescission was time-barred is inconsistent with the facts of this case and is not adopted by this Court.

The purpose of Taiheng Company in acquiring the state-owned construction land use right in question was to develop the land for real estate, and the completion of land demolition was a necessary step for Taiheng Company to develop the land in question. Because the change in regulations prevented Taiheng Company from completing the demolition and consolidation of the land in question, and thus from achieving its contractual purpose of developing the land, Taiheng Company's request to rescind the contract in question is consistent with the actual situation that its contractual purpose could not be achieved. The original court's finding that there was no obstacle to the realization of the contractual purpose is inconsistent with the facts and should be corrected.

(2) The legal consequences of the rescission of the "State-owned Construction Land Use Right Transfer Contract" in question

Article 97 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides that after a contract is rescinded, the performance that has not yet been performed shall be terminated; with respect to what has already been performed, the party may, based on the circumstances of performance and the nature of the contract, demand restoration to the original state, take other remedial measures, and have the right to demand compensation for losses. Therefore, the rescission of a contract includes the legal consequences of restoration to the original state, taking other remedial measures, and compensation for losses. In this case, Taiheng Company's claims include two items: restoration to the original state and compensation for losses. This Court analyzes this as follows:

1. Regarding the Issue of Refund of Land Transfer Fees. Pursuant to Article 97 of the Contract Law of the PRC, after a contract is rescinded, for performance that has already been rendered, the parties may demand restoration to the original status based on the nature of the performance and the circumstances of the contract. Accordingly, where this Court has rendered a judgment rescinding the contract, Taiheng Company's request that the Changchun Bureau of Natural Resources return the state-owned land use right transfer fee it has already paid complies with the above legal provision. Therefore, the Changchun Bureau of Natural Resources shall return the land transfer fee and the statutory interest for the period during which the funds were occupied to Taiheng Company. Given that the land use right transfer fee involved in this case, RMB 26,300,000, was paid in two installments on November 26, 2010 and December 25, 2010 respectively, the Changchun Bureau of Natural Resources shall return to Taiheng Company the land use right transfer fee of RMB 26,300,000 together with the corresponding statutory interest (with RMB 6,000,000 accruing interest from November 26, 2010 until the date of actual payment, and RMB 20,300,000 accruing interest from December 25, 2010 until the date of actual payment, both calculated at the same period comparable demand deposit interest rate of the People's Bank of China).

2. Regarding the Issue of Compensation for Losses. Article 16 of the "State-owned Construction Land Use Right Transfer Contract" involved in this case stipulated that Taiheng Company's construction project on the subject land should commence before November 25, 2011, i.e., the period from the contract signing date of December 25, 2010 to the contractual commencement date of November 25, 2011 was the period for Taiheng Company to carry out demolition and site preparation work on the subject land. However, on January 21, 2011, the State Council issued the "Regulations on the Expropriation of Houses on State-owned Land and Compensation," which resulted in a change in the demolition system. During the contractual demolition period, due to this change in the demolition system, Taiheng Company was unable to obtain a demolition permit and consequently unable to complete the demolition and site preparation work on the subject land. Accordingly, the failure of Taiheng Company to complete the demolition and site preparation work on the subject land within the contractual time limit was not caused by Taiheng Company's fault. The finding of the original trial judgment that Taiheng Company's neglect of its contractual obligations led to the inability to obtain the demolition permit is inconsistent with the facts of this case. Similarly, although the "Notice of the Ministry of Land and Resources and the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development on Further Strengthening the Regulation of Real Estate Land Use and Construction Management" issued on September 21, 2010 stipulated that land should not be transferred in an "undeveloped land" manner, and the "Regulations on the Expropriation of Houses on State-owned Land and Compensation" issued by the State Council on January 21, 2011 provided that the city or county people's government is responsible for house expropriation and compensation work within its administrative region, Article 35 of the same Regulations also provides that projects for which a house demolition permit had been lawfully obtained before the implementation of the Regulations shall continue to follow the original provisions for obtaining permits. Therefore, if Taiheng Company had obtained a demolition permit before the issuance of the "Regulations on the Expropriation of Houses on State-owned Land and Compensation," it could still have proceeded with the demolition and site preparation work on the subject land on its own. However, Taiheng Company failed to apply for a demolition permit within nearly two months, which resulted in its inability to continue obtaining a demolition permit after the implementation of the said Regulations. The Changchun Bureau of Natural Resources is also not at fault in this regard. Given that neither the Changchun Bureau of Natural Resources nor Taiheng Company is at fault for the inability to perform the contract and the frustration of Taiheng Company's contractual purpose, Taiheng Company's claim for compensation for losses from the Changchun Bureau of Natural Resources lacks sufficient grounds and is not supported by this Court.

As for the deed tax of RMB 1,315,000 paid by Taiheng Company to obtain the state-owned land use right involved in this case, since neither party is at fault for the rescission of the contract, this portion of the deed tax may be shared equally between the parties based on the principle of fairness. The Changchun Bureau of Planning and Natural Resources shall compensate Taiheng Company RMB 657,500.

In summary, where a contract between parties cannot be performed due to the issuance of national laws, regulations, and policies, resulting in the frustration of one party's contractual purpose, this Court supports that party's request for a court judgment to rescind the contract. Under such circumstances, given that neither party is at fault for the inability to perform the contract or the frustration of one party's contractual purpose, this Court, pursuant to Article 97 of the Contract Law of the PRC concerning the parties' right to demand restoration to the original status after contract rescission, only orders the Changchun Bureau of Natural Resources to return the land transfer fee paid by Taiheng Company and the statutory interest. Taiheng Company's claim for compensation for losses from the Changchun Bureau of Natural Resources is not supported. Therefore, the factual findings and legal application of the courts of first and second instance are both erroneous and shall be corrected. Pursuant to Article 170, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 407, Paragraph 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this Court hereby renders the following judgment:

1. The Civil Judgment (2018) Ji Min Zhong No. 264 of the Jilin High People's Court and the Civil Judgment (2017) Ji 01 Min Chu No. 227 of the Changchun Intermediate People's Court are hereby vacated.

2. Effective upon the entry into force of this judgment, the "State-owned Construction Land Use Right Transfer Contract" signed between the Changchun Bureau of Land and Resources (subsequently renamed the Changchun Bureau of Planning and Natural Resources) and Changchun Taiheng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. on November 25, 2010 is hereby rescinded.

3. The Changchun Bureau of Planning and Natural Resources shall, within thirty days of the entry into force of this judgment, return RMB 26,300,000 and interest to Changchun Taiheng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (with RMB 6,000,000 accruing interest from November 26, 2010, and RMB 20,300,000 accruing interest from December 25, 2010, both calculated at the demand deposit interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period until the date of actual payment).

4. The Changchun Bureau of Planning and Natural Resources shall, within thirty days of the entry into force of this judgment, compensate Changchun Taiheng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. RMB 657,500.

5. All other claims of Changchun Taiheng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. are dismissed.

If the obligation to pay a sum of money is not performed within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

Court acceptance fee of first instance: RMB 229,058, to be borne by the Changchun Bureau of Planning and Natural Resources in the amount of RMB 114,529 and by Changchun Taiheng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 114,529. Court acceptance fee of second instance: RMB 229,058, to be borne by the Changchun Bureau of Planning and Natural Resources in the amount of RMB 114,529 and by Changchun Taiheng Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 114,529.

This judgment is final.
